title: The sheafified free presheaf on a representable with flat coefficients is flat (j_{X!} of a constant flat sheaf is flat)
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be an essentially small category with a Grothendieck topology $J$, and let $\mathcal A$ be a Grothendieck abelian category with a symmetric monoidal closed structure whose tensor product is additive in each variable; give $\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C,J;\mathcal A)$ the sheafified objectwise tensor product. Let $P$ be an object of $\mathcal A$ such that $P\otimes-:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$ preserves finite limits, let $X$ be an object of $\mathcal C$, and let $P_X^\#$ be the sheaf associated to the presheaf $V\mapsto\bigoplus_{\varphi\in\mathrm{Mor}_{\mathcal C}(V,X)}P$ (restriction along $\psi:V'\to V$ sending the summand of $\varphi$ to that of $\varphi\psi$ by the identity); equivalently $P_X^\#=j_{X!}\underline P_X$, the extension by zero of the constant sheaf $P$ on $\mathcal C/X$. Then $P_X^\#\otimes-:\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C,J;\mathcal A)\to\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C,J;\mathcal A)$ preserves finite limits.

source.place: Lemma 03EV (lemma-j-shriek-flat): j_{U!}O_U is flat, proved via Lemma 03ES (lemma-flatness-presheaves: objectwise flat presheaves are flat), Lemma 03ET (lemma-flatness-sheafification) and Lemma 0GMW (lemma-sheafification-tensor); description of j_{U!} as sheafification of V -> sum over Mor(V,U), Lemma 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero); projection formula Lemma 0E8I (lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor). Stacks treats O-modules; the A-valued statement is the flatness claim of the module docstring ('The sheaf case') of WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.GrothendieckAbelian.Monoidal.FlatResolution (slopmaster2), no Lean declaration. Intended proof (agent, generalizing 03EV): by [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-tensor-closed] (2), P_X^# (x) F = a(Q (x)_p iota F) for Q the presheaf above; (Q (x)_p G)(V) = sum over Mor(V,X) of P (x) G(V) since - (x) G(V) preserves coproducts (closed); finite limits of presheaves are objectwise, P (x) - is left exact and coproducts in A are exact (AB4, from AB5), so G -> Q (x)_p G is left exact on presheaves; iota is a right adjoint and a is exact, so F -> a(Q (x)_p iota F) is left exact

proof.text: Step 1 (the functor to be studied). Let $Q$ be the presheaf $V\mapsto\bigoplus_{\varphi\in\mathrm{Mor}_{\mathcal C}(V,X)}P$ of the statement, so $P_X^\#=aQ$, and let $\iota$, $a$, $\otimes_p$ be as in [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-tensor-closed]. By the definition of the sheaf tensor product in [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-tensor-closed] (2), $P_X^\#\otimes F=a(\iota aQ\otimes_p\iota F)$, and by the strong monoidality of $a$ in the same clause, $a(Q\otimes_p\iota F)\cong aQ\otimes a(\iota F)$ naturally in the sheaf $F$. The counit $a\iota F\to F$ is an isomorphism, naturally in $F$ ([lem-weil-pbc-presheaf-finite-limits-objectwise] (3)), and $aQ\otimes-$ is a functor, so $P_X^\#\otimes F\cong a(Q\otimes_p\iota F)$ naturally in $F$. Hence $P_X^\#\otimes-\cong a\circ(Q\otimes_p-)\circ\iota$ as functors $\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C,J;\mathcal A)\to\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C,J;\mathcal A)$, and since a functor naturally isomorphic to one preserving finite limits preserves them, it suffices to show that $a\circ(Q\otimes_p-)\circ\iota$ preserves finite limits. (In Stacks this is the identification $j_{U!}\mathcal O_U=(j_{U!}\mathcal O_U)^\#$ together with Lemma 0GMW, $\mathcal F^\#\otimes\mathcal G^\#=(\mathcal F\otimes_p\mathcal G)^\#$; for $\mathcal A$-valued sheaves the strong monoidality of $a$ is the clause of [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-tensor-closed] that replaces 0GMW.)

source.place: Lemma 03EV (lemma-j-shriek-flat), proof of (2), and Lemma 0GMW (lemma-sheafification-tensor); generalization to A-valued sheaves by the agent

proof.text: Step 2 (the values of $Q$ are flat in $\mathcal A$). Fix an object $V$ of $\mathcal C$. $\mathrm{Mor}_{\mathcal C}(V,X)$ is a set ($\mathcal C$ is essentially small, in particular locally small), and $\mathcal A$, being Grothendieck abelian, has coproducts indexed by sets, so $Q(V)=\coprod_{\varphi\in\mathrm{Mor}_{\mathcal C}(V,X)}P$ exists. $\mathcal A$ is Grothendieck abelian with a symmetric, hence braided, monoidal closed structure, and each summand $P$ is flat ($P\otimes-$ preserves finite limits, by hypothesis). By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-coproduct] applied to $\mathcal B=\mathcal A$ and the constant family $P$ indexed by $\mathrm{Mor}_{\mathcal C}(V,X)$, $Q(V)$ is flat: $Q(V)\otimes-:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$ preserves finite limits. (If $\mathrm{Mor}(V,X)=\emptyset$ then $Q(V)=0$ and $0\otimes-\cong0$, which preserves finite limits; this is the empty case of the same lemma.) Concretely, the argument of that lemma is the one asked for here: since $\otimes$ is closed, $-\otimes G$ is a left adjoint and $Q(V)\otimes G\cong\bigoplus_{\varphi}P\otimes G$ naturally in $G$; $P\otimes-$ preserves finite limits; and coproducts in $\mathcal A$ are exact (AB4, implied by AB5), so a coproduct of left exact functors is left exact. This replaces Stacks' remark that $\bigoplus_\varphi\mathcal O(V)$ is a flat $\mathcal O(V)$-module (a direct sum of flat modules is flat): in a general $\mathcal A$ it needs the closed structure and AB4, not only the definition of flatness.

source.place: Lemma 03EV (lemma-j-shriek-flat), proof of (1): j_{U!}O_U(V) is the direct sum over Mor(V,U) of O(V), a flat O(V)-module (formula from Remark remark-localize-presheaves, line 2288); generalization to A by the agent

proof.text: Step 3 (the presheaf tensor product with $Q$ is left exact). Consider $Q\otimes_p-:\mathrm{PSh}(\mathcal C;\mathcal A)\to\mathrm{PSh}(\mathcal C;\mathcal A)$, $G\mapsto Q\otimes_pG$, with $(Q\otimes_pG)(V)=Q(V)\otimes G(V)$ and $(Q\otimes_pg)_V=Q(V)\otimes g_V$ for a morphism $g$ of presheaves. For every object $V$, $\mathrm{ev}_V\circ(Q\otimes_p-)=(Q(V)\otimes-)\circ\mathrm{ev}_V$ (by the definition of $\otimes_p$). $\mathcal A$ is abelian, so it has finite limits, and $\mathrm{ev}_V$ preserves finite limits ([lem-weil-pbc-presheaf-finite-limits-objectwise] (1)); $Q(V)\otimes-$ preserves finite limits (Step 2); so their composite does. By [lem-weil-pbc-presheaf-finite-limits-objectwise] (1) (finite limits of presheaves are objectwise), $Q\otimes_p-$ preserves finite limits. (This is Stacks 03ES, 'immediate from the definitions', for $\mathcal A$-valued presheaves.)

source.place: Lemma 03ES (lemma-flatness-presheaves): a presheaf with flat values is flat, proof 'immediate from the definitions', written out for A-valued presheaves by the agent

proof.text: Step 4 (conclusion). $\iota$ preserves finite limits ([lem-weil-pbc-presheaf-finite-limits-objectwise] (2)); $Q\otimes_p-$ preserves finite limits (Step 3); $a$ is exact, in particular preserves finite limits ([lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-tensor-closed] (1), which is stated for $\mathcal A$-valued sheaves on an essentially small site, so the abelian-group node lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact is not needed). A composite of functors preserving finite limits preserves finite limits, so $a\circ(Q\otimes_p-)\circ\iota$ does, and by Step 1 so does $P_X^\#\otimes-$. (This is the hint of Stacks 03ET, 'sheafification is exact', for the sheafification of the flat presheaf of Step 3.)

One new Mathlib leaf: lem-weil-pbc-presheaf-finite-limits-objectwise (preservesFiniteLimits_of_evaluation, sheafToPresheaf preserves finite limits, counit iso).
